_comment: OPTIONAL, AND NOT CONFIRMED ON HARDWARE. On firmware 1.50+ the board becomes two game controllers with a fixed internal pin-to-button map simply by switching to mode 2 (hold Start1+P1SW2 for 10 seconds), no config involved. This file is for the other case: choosing which button each pin sends, which needs mode 4 (Start1+P1SW4) - the Dinput mode that acts on the config. Mode 2 ignores it.
_sticks_note: Stick pins (1up/1down/1left/1right, 2up/...) carry a description but no action on purpose. Pins a profile does not assign an action keep whatever the board already has, so this file will not break your sticks - but see _incomplete_note for what that costs. The descriptions record what Batocera expects each direction to be; HAT 1 on all four is the value confirmed to make EmulationStation read them as a d-pad.
_description_note: "description" is a label only. It is what the web UI shows next to the pin; the board is programmed from "action". Both players send GAMEPAD 1..12 because in Dinput mode each player is a separate controller and the two share one code range - the GP1/GP2 prefix is for the reader, not the board.
_incomplete_note: This template cannot trigger Ultimarc's automatic mode switch, because it is not gamepad-only once encoded. The board switches to mode 4 by itself only when the whole 256-byte download is gamepad actions, and this file leaves the eight stick pins unassigned and never clears the alternate (shifted) actions - so applied to a factory board, fifteen keycodes survive and the download is mixed. `apply` says so. Either finish the file, or switch mode by hand with Start1+P1SW4.
_hotkey_warning: Confirmed on hardware: written as-is in keyboard mode, this file leaves the board unable to switch modes. Start1+P1SW1-5 needs 1start (the shift key) and 1sw1..1sw5, and this file puts GAMEPAD actions on all six - which do nothing in keyboard mode. The way back is holding P1SW1 while plugging in usb. `apply` warns about this before writing.
_numbering_note: GAMEPAD n here means what WinIPAC calls 'P1 Button n' and what the host sees as button n. GAMEPAD 1 is 0x8e. Earlier versions of ipacconf numbered from 0x90, so this file used to send button 3 where it said GAMEPAD 1; corrected against hardware, see README.md.
